elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 7(a) caps both sides: "CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO ..." and "COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO ..."; both now run to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap is "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — it uses "paid" only (not "paid or payable") and contains no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor or "greater of" construction.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 7(b) retained unchanged: "NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS ... ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS", and Excluded Claims are expressly "UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Excluded Claims definition lists only indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are carved out.
"EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS", stated to be uncapped for either party; this no longer depends on the ambiguous "PARAGRAPH 9" cross-reference.
Excluded Claims expressly include "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT", uncapped for either party.
Excluded Claims expressly include "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT", uncapped for either party.
Fraud does not appear anywhere in the Excluded Claims definition or elsewhere in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the Excluded Claims definition; only the pre-existing "PARAGRAPH 9" exception (Independent Contractor clause) remains, which is not an IP carve-out.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in 7(a)/(b) states that Company's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; Company's cap remains a flat limit on "MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON".

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Both the Contractor sentence and the Company sentence in 7(a) impose a maximum liability limit; mutuality pre-existed and is preserved.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Both caps re-based to "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM", replacing the open-ended "FEES PAID ... FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES" basis.
New definition: "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...", carved out of the cap and "UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breach is included in the Excluded Claims definition, which the 7(a) lead-in excepts from both caps.
"ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" is within Excluded Claims and thus outside the cap for either party.
Willful misconduct is expressly named in the Excluded Claims definition and carved out of both caps.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: mutuality was already present, the basis is now expressly twelve (12) months of fees paid, and a mutual Excluded Claims definition places indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside both caps.
The carve-out is operative for both sentences because the inserted lead-in states Excluded Claims "ARE UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY", so the Company-cap sentence is not left contradicting the exception.

Preferred remains unmet on five items the drafter must add if pressing the preferred position: (i) "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor; (ii) "paid or payable" rather than "paid"; (iii) data protection and security obligations in Excluded Claims; (iv) fraud and infringement of the other party's IP in Excluded Claims; (v) an express statement that Company's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are the cap-basis words "FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES", which are the target of the 12-months-of-fees element; the favourable Paragraph 9 exception, the Statement-of-Work scoping of Contractor's cap and the mutual 7(b) exclusion are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved: the pre-existing (and pre-existing ambiguous) "PARAGRAPH 9" cross-reference is untouched rather than newly created, no defined term is left dangling, and the asymmetry favouring Company (Contractor's cap scoped to SOW Services) survives.
